entries.title: First C-Walk Video
entries.description: The first experience I had with learning to dance was C-Walking. At the time, I had discovered an online community of people on YouTube where people would share their practice on there, and I felt drawn since it seemed like a lot of asian diaspora people were doing this, so I watched tutorials and shared my own C-Walking videos https://youtu.be/PQ-daAx4qJ0

entries.title: C-Walk crew tryout video
entries.description: I joined an online crew called [N]erdiie [A]zn [C]lown [W]alkerz https://youtu.be/d0qSYPQeDok

entries.title: Imagine Music Festival 2018
entries.description: This was my first time seeing shuffle dancers at a music festival and this moment kind of planted a seed in my mind of my desire to learn how to shuffle one day, so that at another festival, I could be in the crowd shuffling like the friends I made at this festival who inspired me, specifically my camping neighbors :)

entries.title: Imagine Festival 2019
entries.description: Acknowledged and further solidified my desire to learn shuffle dance for next music festival - I had planned to go to another festival in the spring of the next year, and I set a goal for myself that I would join a shuffle circle there. It was supposed to be at Ubbi Dubbi in Texas, which eventually got canceled because of covid, which also then led me to continue to learn shuffling anyways because of the pandemic. :)

entries.title: First shuffle challenge: shuffle fitness
entries.description: Participating in this shuffle challenge is what I consider the true start to my shuffle dance journey, since it was the point in time where I was in a mindset where I was intentionally learning and practicing the dance in a consistent way. In this challenge, the moderators of an Instagram account would post a move/combo each day, and the challenge was for the participants to learn from the tutorials they provided, and post on their own Instagram story

entries.title: Posted first shuffle reel
entries.description: Inspired by a Sterling Torres' reel, where I learned a flow she did to On Your Mind by Kaskade https://www.instagram.com/reel/CENf-Ckl-oa/

entries.title: First injury, sprained ankle
entries.description: The first time I had an injury that had affected me greatly because of how it relates to myself and dancing was a sprained ankle - had a misstep walking down the stairs from a trip to Berlin back to Weimar. This was the first moment I think I can remember my mental health being negatively affected because of dance -- or maybe rather the lack of it in this context. Maybe not only because I'd gotten the dopamine from the physical practice itself, but also possibly because of the dopamine hits from the affirmations online, since I was primarily connecting with other dancers online.

entries.title: First time participating in a music video!
entries.description: Mark Dekoda - Rave Harder Techno Bass https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aKA8GrteDM One of my highlights of my time in Vienna, where I connected with other shufflers in real life for the first time. EXIL Club, Vienna, AT

entries.title: Second (online) tournament participation: WSC
entries.description: Prelims: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Ci8GQGeIDkc/ Round 1: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Ckbc54yoAzy/ “Made it past prelims, lost in round 1 to Marcel/Lotus”

entries.title: First experience watching a dance battle in person
entries.description: house dance, djoon club (Paris, FR). An aha moment on what it's like to experience these types of community events and that I love them. Validating moments when I would join dance circles, and people would dap me up afterwards, giving me respect about my flow

entries.title: TSL 2023
entries.description: “Beginning of a core shuffle-identity crisis of mine: which country do I represent at competitions? Marbiik filmed clips of each country's shufflers, and they'd done the US one without me, and I appeared in the French and German/Swiss ones, fueled/incepted the identity crisis in a way”

entries.title: First paid collab! Music video with irredrecords
entries.description: Validating experience for someone to reach out to me, thinking that they'd want my dancing as a part of something.

entries.title: Riot of Rhythm Tournament (Berlin)
entries.description: - Made it into the bracket - Didn't make it past the 1st round - matchups made by participants choosing their opponents

entries.title: Summer shuffle Cup (Warsaw)
entries.description: - Made it into the bracket! - Didn't make it past the 1st round

entries.title: TSL 2024
entries.description: (Written on 01.03.2025) I know while I was there and experiencing it, it felt different but I wasn't sure why - I think for sure because of my health situations - but maybe as an extension this break I had for health kind of distanced me from my relationship with dance and led me to experience the event differently. Also my sense of belonging felt definitely weirder than the year before. In 2023 I wasn't called to be a part of the videos they were filming for the US shufflers, but I was a part of the French & German ones, and this year I didn't feel so connected with the US crowd too - they'd hype each other up, and I felt urges to run over and join but held myself back because to some extent I didn't feel a part of their community, and though I felt this trip was great in terms of me feeling closer with the German community, to some extent I wasn't sure how much I was a part of it either... Maybe the world cup concept doesn't fit for me? Where people are categorized by country

entries.title: First US Battle: TC Battles
entries.description: Miami, FL, USA. Accomplishment! Made it past the first round, something I hadn't accomplished yet in previous battles. A shuffler who I enjoy watching said she liked my style. No qualification rounds, it was a first come first serve into the 32-person bracket. Interesting thing about this battle was that there was no limit to how long someone's round would be - you could dance as long as you wanted for your round. Round 1 vs OzzyModo. Round 2 vs Krisis (Trance Track)

entries.title: First Janeiro on spin
entries.description: I got my first Janeiro on spin pole :) was just for a couple of seconds, felt great though, didn't know what to transition to afterwards

entries.title: First Flying Pole Class
entries.description:
Lea encouraged me to try out her flying pole class since I was progressing well in her handstand handspring class so I tried it out :)

Practiced entries, handsprings and getting used to the spinning in general
entries.notes: Loved it!! I feel like trying this out is inner child healing work kind of, since freshman year in high school I'd always been curious about the cirque program at school, especially aerial silks, but didn't have the courage to try it out. Really fulfilling :)

entries.title: First handspring!!
entries.description:
Class with Mary

Got my first handspring(s) without needing a spot 🥹
entries.notes:
was both in cup and twisted grip :D felt super nice that I could get this advanced trick 6 months into my pole practice. 

the wrist strength I'd built from bouldering for sure helped get me there

entries.title: First House Dance Class
entries.description: Joined Thuy & friends to a class Sharxilla was teaching. Don't remember what type of class but it was probably fundamentals or something like that
entries.notes: Looking back on it now, going to classes with other dance friends (in this context shuffle friends) was a way that made me feel at home and part of a community in Paris, contributed to my sense of belonging 😌

entries.title: First pole class (Absolute Beginner's)
entries.description: Took my first pole class -- the fact that it was called "Introduction to the Pole Dance life..New members Absolute Beginner's" and that a man was the instructor all contributed to me feeling comfortable enough to try it out. I think we did basic spins and climbs.
entries.notes:
The start of a new dance practice after some time of feeling a bit disconnected with my "main" one (shuffling)

The videos I watched a while back of boulderers trying pole dance and pole dancers trying bouldering definitely influenced my decision to try this out. Great decision and added so much to my life in Berlin and appreciation and awareness of my body and its capabilities :)
